idiom_name: ViewModifier with .modifier(_:), @ViewBuilder wrapper views and environment injection
implementation_notes: SwiftUI's ViewModifier is documented as a modifier that you apply to a view or another view modifier, producing a different version of the original value - exactly the pattern's mechanic: a type whose body(content:) receives the wrapped view and returns the enhanced one, applied with .modifier(_:) without editing the wrapped view. A generic wrapper view (struct WithX<Content: View> with a @ViewBuilder initialiser) covers the cases where the enhancer must own state or inject environment values, and .environment(_:_:) is the ambient-injection channel that replaces prop threading. The hand-written wrapper view remains the right choice when the enhancement must exist as a node - state ownership, layout, navigation containers - rather than as a modifier.
pitfalls: View identity: a wrapper or modifier whose type changes between renders changes the view's structural identity and resets its @State - keep the wrapper type stable and vary its values instead.
A ViewModifier cannot reach into the wrapped view; it can only wrap environment, layout and effects around it, so enhancements that need the view's internals are not expressible as a modifier.
Environment propagation is implicit and shadowing: a nested wrapper that sets the same environment key overrides the outer value for everything below it.
